narrative.overview:
The console publishes the team's memory the way a consolidated code of practice is published: a contents of everything a member can reach, each memory set as a citable section, and its standing, author and history annotated in a ruled margin. Light is the printed page; dark is the bound volume. Paper and ink carry nearly everything, and a single buckram green is the binding: it draws the rules that set things off, marks the current place, and carries links and primary actions.

The density is that of a reference book, not a dashboard. A slim masthead, a contents column in a slightly deeper paper, and a reading column held to a book measure. Weight is carried by typographic rank (serif against sans, upright against italic, whole against struck through), never by colour fields, cards or badges. Hairline rules, dot leaders and heads hanging into the margin do the structural work that boxes and shadows do elsewhere.

The system refuses the admin-dashboard arrangement: no sidebar of features, no stat cards, no badge soup. Nothing disappears; superseded and retired memory keeps its place, visibly cancelled. Motion is limited to state changes on one soft ease-out, and reduced motion is honoured.
keyCharacteristics: Paper and ink in two bindings, the printed page (light) and the bound volume (dark), both tinted toward green and never neutral grey.
One structural accent, buckram green, for rules, the current place, links and primary actions.
Source Serif 4 for what is read, Public Sans for what is operated, the system monospace for paths and source.
Square corners, hairline rules, dot leaders, part heads hanging into the margin.
State is a mark and a word; the weight of a memory is type rank.
Flat: depth comes from steps of paper and from rules, not from shadow.

rules.name: The Binding Rule
rules.body: Buckram green is the binding, not a paint: it draws rules, marks the current place and carries links and primary actions. It fills nothing larger than a button or the waiting count; the only green surfaces are the pale washes that mark where you are, what was inserted, or a token just issued.

rules.name: The Mark-and-Word Rule
rules.body: State is a mark and a word, never a hue alone. Red never appears without an icon and a sentence, and green never signals a status by itself.

rules.name: The Third-Ink Rule
rules.body: Third ink is for text on paper and paper-2 only (5.1:1 and 4.8:1 on the printed page). On paper-3 or a wash it falls under 4.5:1, so text set on those steps up to second ink.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: The serif carries what is read: memory text, the names of memories, folders and parts, page titles, standfirsts and the wordmark. The sans carries what is operated: controls, labels, metadata and tables. A memory's name is serif wherever it appears, even as a leaf in the contents column.

rules.name: The Rank-Not-Hue Rule
rules.body: A memory's weight is set in type. Accepted memory is upright at 620; personal memory is italic at 450 over a dashed rule; superseded and retired memory is struck through at 450 in third ink. No colour does this work.

rules.name: The Figures Rule
rules.body: Counts, dates and times take tabular figures; figures inside memory text are oldstyle and proportional.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Memory text never runs wider than 68ch, and lists of contents read at 72ch. Wide registers scroll sideways inside their own container, never the page.

rules.name: The Hanging Head Rule
rules.body: Part heads in a folder hang 18px into the left margin, and every level below steps in 18px (12px at 900px and below), so the structure reads from the left edge like a code's numbered divisions.

rules.name: The Leader Rule
rules.body: A name and its figures are joined by a dotted leader (1px dotted third ink at 45 to 60% opacity, lifted 4px onto the baseline). Under 600px the leader drops and the figures wrap beneath the name.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the page casts a shadow. Separation is a hairline rule or a step of paper; a shadow is reserved for a menu that floats above the page.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Every corner is square. A framework part that insists on a radius gets no more than 2px.

rules.name: The Line Weights Rule
rules.body: A 1px solid rule divides parts; a 1px dotted rule divides items within a set and draws leaders; a 1px dashed rule marks personal memory the team hasn't accepted; a 2px buckram rule sets off a notice or the title page and underlines the current place; a 1px ink rule closes a register's header.

dos: **Do** reference colour through the custom properties (`var(--paper)`, `var(--ink-2)`, `var(--accent)`) so both bindings follow, and point framework components at them rather than at the framework's own palette.
**Do** set memory text in Source Serif 4 at 1.125rem and 1.65 within 68ch, exactly as stored.

**Do** give every state a mark and a word: a dagger, "Superseded" and a struck title; "Retired" and a struck title; the scales icon and "Challenged"; the pin and "Pinned"; the lock and "Restricted"; italic, a dashed rule and a banner for personal memory.
**Do** keep cancelled memory in its place, after current memory, struck through in third ink.
**Do** join a name to its figures with a dotted leader and set counts and dates in tabular figures.
**Do** show loading as the shape of what is coming, in shimmering bars of paper.

**Do** keep motion to state changes on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`: 150ms for colour and underlines, 180ms for a folder's chevron, 220ms for a notice or slip to appear (fade and a 4px rise), and honour reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** build the admin-dashboard arrangement: no sidebar of features, no stat cards, no badge soup. The waiting count on Challenges is the only filled chip.
**Don't** let colour alone carry a state, and don't use oxide red for anything but refusals, challenges and actions that take something away.
**Don't** round corners, add shadows to cards, or box content that a rule could separate.
**Don't** use neutral greys: every paper, ink and rule leans green (OKLCH hue roughly 130 to 170).
**Don't** set the uppercase label style above a title as a kicker; labels name data (margin terms, table columns, the contents column), they never announce a heading.
**Don't** use a Unicode symbol as an icon. Icons are drawn outline icons; the dagger is the one typographic mark, set in the serif beside a struck title and the word Superseded.
**Don't** restyle, truncate or paraphrase a memory's words on its own page; summaries belong to lists.
